Plot input versus effective sample size of compositions

Source: R/plot_composition_diagnostics.R
plot_composition_samples.Rd

Compare the input (or adjusted input) sample size of each composition with its effective sample size, the sample size implied by how well the model fits the composition. This is the diagnostic behind the McAllister and Ianelli (1997) data weighting method.

plot_composition_samples(
  dat,
  comp_type = NULL,
  fleet = NULL,
  show_years = FALSE,
  ncol = NULL,
  direction = "v"
)

Arguments

dat

A tibble returned from convert_output() that contains composition data (see bigskate_lencomp), or composition data in any other format accepted by prepare_composition_data(). For Stock Synthesis output converted from a Report.sso file without compositions by bin, the adjusted input (nsamp_adj) and effective (effn) sample sizes in the FIT_LEN_COMPS and FIT_AGE_COMPS tables are used instead (as in stockplotr::example_data).

comp_type

String. Type of composition to keep when dat contains more than one. Options: "age", "length", or NULL (keep all). Default: NULL

fleet

Character or numeric vector. Fleet(s) to keep, matching either the fleet name (e.g., "Fishery_current") or the fleet name with its partition (e.g., "Fishery_current (retained)"). NULL keeps all fleets. Default: NULL

show_years

Logical. TRUE/FALSE; label each point with its year. Default: FALSE

ncol

Number. Number of facet columns. NULL lets ggplot2 choose. Default: NULL

direction

String. Order of the panels: "v" fills panels down each column and then across, so consecutive years are stacked vertically and cohorts are easier to follow from panel to panel; "h" fills panels across each row.

Default: "v"

Value

A ggplot2 object.

Details

For each composition (year and fleet), the effective sample size is $$N_{eff} = \sum_b e_b (1 - e_b) / \sum_b (o_b - e_b)^2$$ where \(o_b\) and \(e_b\) are the observed and expected proportions in bin \(b\) (McAllister and Ianelli 1997), the same calculation used by Stock Synthesis.

Each panel shows a 1:1 line, a loess smoother (dashed red, when there are more than six distinct input sample sizes), the arithmetic mean of the input sample sizes (vertical dashed line), and the harmonic mean of the effective sample sizes (horizontal dashed line). The ratio of the harmonic mean effective sample size to the mean input sample size, the McAllister-Ianelli weight, is included in each panel label. Ratios below one suggest that input sample sizes are too large relative to the fit. As in Stock Synthesis, the weight is calculated across all partitions of a fleet; multiplying it by the current variance adjustment gives the Recommend_var_adj reported by Stock Synthesis.

Effective sample sizes from this formula are not appropriate for compositions fit with a Dirichlet-multinomial likelihood.

Equivalent plots in other packages

r4ss: r4ss::SSplotComps() subplot 7 ("N-EffN comparison").

References

McAllister, M.K., and Ianelli, J.N. (1997). Bayesian stock assessment using catch-age data and the sampling-importance resampling algorithm. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 54: 284-300.

See also

prepare_composition_data(), plot_composition_francis()

Examples

plot_composition_samples(bigskate_lencomp)


# Stock Synthesis output converted with convert_output()
plot_composition_samples(stockplotr::example_data, comp_type = "length")
